reports.name: USDA Weekly Export Sales (delayed by Veterans Day)

outlook: Grains were mostly a little lower overnight as the U.S. dollar index hit a 19-month high after this week's hotter-than-expected inflation data. As of early Thursday, December corn was up about a quarter cent, January soybeans were down about 1 1/4 cents, December Chicago wheat was off 1 1/2 cents and December Minneapolis spring wheat was down about 3 3/4 cents near $6.32. Wheat traders are watching reports that China is looking for more wheat after buying French wheat this week, and the end of Russia–Ukraine peace talks without a breakthrough; South American crop weather is seen as favorable. ICE January canola rose about C$11 to near C$781.50 per tonne in overnight trade. Cash bids below are from Wednesday's Minneapolis report; Thursday's report comes out after the close.
